line: Aurelio Mendoza. I'm president of the Club Jerez, the families from Jerez, Zacatecas. We meet here. Forty-two families. You're not from Jerez.
choice1: No, but I'd like to hear about it.
choice3: Does it matter where I'm from?

line: Last year the Club paid for a new roof on the clinic in Jerez. Raffles, a dance, plates of food. No city, no grants, no forms. Our money, our roof.
Thirty-four years I was a pipefitter in this city. I know how it works. They give you a little, then they come with a clipboard. What's ours, we keep ours.
Maybe. But the kids who go to the city programs, I don't see them here after. The Club needs people who come back. Do you come back?
choice2: I go a lot of places.

line: The Club's dance is in three weeks. The band from Fresno wants double this year. I said, for double, play twice as long. They said no.
Doctor says walk after lunch, so I walk. Two laps. Look at those two at the chess table, the same game every day. In Jerez we play dominoes, and loud.
You're serious, I can tell. So listen. Pilar wants the city in here with forms. Ray wants us all to be Raymond. I want there to be a here. Somebody has to.
choice2: Maybe there's room for all three.

line: Saturday the Club's board has dinner at my house. My wife makes birria. I want you there, sitting with the young ones who will run this after me.
You see? When Washington gets nervous, it's us they look at. That's why the Club has its own fund for lawyers. Nobody had to give us permission.
Everyone is happy with the new president. Good. Enjoy. Presidents change. The Club has been here since 1989.
You're here so much the ladies ask if you're somebody's nephew. I tell them yes. Don't make me a liar.
Ah. The library one. Pilar tells me you're over there more and more. That's fine. Just remember who fed you first.
choice1: I still come here, Don Aurelio.
I spoke out of turn before. I'm sorry.

line: Not now, I'm waiting for the treasurer. She's always late, and always right.
